Earth is tiny compared to what exists beyond it.

Human civilization currently uses only a microscopic fraction of the Sun’s energy. Even if humanity increased its energy usage a million times over, it would still be almost nothing compared to the scale and power of the Sun.

The Sun contains roughly 99.8% of the mass in the entire solar system. Everything else, including Earth, is incredibly small in comparison.

Musk believes this is why civilization cannot remain Earth-bound forever. The long-term future of humanity depends on expanding into space where energy, resources and growth potential exist at an almost unimaginable scale.

For a truly advanced civilization, space is not a side project. It’s the next frontier.

Elon Musk says space-based data centers may be far more achievable than most people realize.

Musk pointed to SpaceX already operating around 10,000 satellites in orbit today, with Starship expected to eventually launch more than 10,000 next-generation communication satellites every year.

He says future satellite capability could increase global space-based communications capacity by 100x compared to today.

But according to Musk, even that could be small compared to what comes next: massive AI-focused satellite infrastructure and data centers operating directly in space.

The scale of what Starship could enable is difficult to fully comprehend.

🚨FYI: CJ is Neuralink Patient #24. A ventilator-dependent quadriplegic who volunteered for the PRIME trial not for himself, but so Neuralink and the FDA can learn more about N1 technology and help others.

He needs to be back in Miami next month for a required in-person visit. Neuralink denied his request to attend virtually.

Because he is on a ventilator, commercial flights are not an option. His only way there is an air ambulance costing between $38,000 and $52,000 one way.

This man chose to participate in one of the most important medical trials in history so future patients could benefit. The least we can do is help get him there.
